**About Us:**

ESP Safety Inc. is a manufacturer of industrial flame and gas detection systems serving the oil and gas, energy, petrochemical, and industrial markets worldwide.

**About the Role**

We are seeking an experienced, hands\-on Buyer / Production Planner to manage production requirements, material planning, purchasing, and inventory availability at our Santa Clara manufacturing facility.

The successful candidate will work directly with our manufacturing team to translate customer sales orders into production requirements, identify material shortages, and ensure components are available to support manufacturing schedules.

This position requires someone who can independently manage both production planning and purchasing, rather than specializing in only one of these functions.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Production Planning**

* Review open customer sales orders and identify outstanding manufacturing requirements.

**Purchasing \& Material Planning**

* Calculate material shortages based on production requirements, available inventory, and incoming materials.
* Prepare purchase orders and coordinate supplier deliveries.
* Monitor open purchase orders, supplier lead times, and material availability.
* Expedite critical components to support production schedules.
* Coordinate purchasing priorities with Production and Finance.

**Inventory \& ERP Reconciliation**

* Verify inventory availability and investigate discrepancies between physical inventory and ERP records.
* Review outstanding purchase orders and identify incorrect, duplicate, or outdated records.
* Reconcile production requirements with existing Pending Builds and inventory commitments.
* Maintain accurate purchasing and material planning information.
* Assist with implementing and improving inventory and production planning procedures.
* Review existing assembly builds and create or update Pending Builds in QuickBooks Enterprise.
* Plan production quantities and coordinate manufacturing schedules with the Production Manager.
* Work with multi\-level bills of materials (BOMs) and manufacturing assemblies.
* Identify component requirements across multiple production orders.

**Required Qualifications**

* Hands\-on experience in both production planning and purchasing within a manufacturing environment.
* Experience working with multi\-level BOMs, manufacturing work orders, and material requirements planning.
* Experience managing purchase orders and supplier delivery schedules.
* Ability to independently identify material shortages and verify inventory availability.
* Experience with manufacturing ERP systems and inventory reconciliation.
* Strong Excel and analytical skills.
* Ability to work full\-time on\-site in Santa Clara.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with QuickBooks Enterprise manufacturing and inventory functions.
* Background in electronics, instrumentation, industrial equipment, or electromechanical manufacturing.
* Experience improving manufacturing planning and purchasing processes.

**What We Are Looking For**

We are looking for a hands\-on professional who can independently manage production and purchasing requirements, investigate inventory discrepancies, and work directly with our manufacturing team to ensure materials are available when needed.

The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a manufacturing environment where accurate planning requires both ERP analysis and verification of actual inventory and supplier commitments.

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

**Work Location:** Santa Clara, California — On\-site.

ESP Safety is an equal opportunity employer.

Job Type: Full\-time

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $90,000\.00 per year

Application Question(s):

* 1\. Describe your experience in production planning for a manufacturing company.

A. I have independently managed production planning from customer orders through work orders, material requirements, and production scheduling.

B. I have managed production schedules and work orders but relied on another department for material planning.

C. I have performed material planning based on production schedules prepared by others.

D. I have supervised production planning teams but have limited hands\-on planning experience.

E. I have no direct manufacturing production planning experience.

* 2\. Describe your experience with purchasing and purchase order management.

A. I have independently managed purchasing based on production requirements, including identifying shortages, creating POs, managing suppliers, and tracking deliveries.

B. I have managed purchasing and suppliers but received material requirements from a separate planning department.

C. I have prepared POs and followed up with suppliers based on purchasing instructions from others.

D. I have supervised purchasing activities but have limited hands\-on purchasing experience.

E. I have no direct manufacturing purchasing experience.

* 3\. Describe your experience managing production and purchasing when ERP inventory and purchasing records are inaccurate or incomplete.

A. I have independently established production and purchasing requirements by reconciling sales orders, work orders, BOMs, physical inventory, and supplier commitments before relying on ERP reports.

B. I have independently investigated inventory and purchasing discrepancies and corrected the records before using ERP reports for planning.

C. I have identified discrepancies and worked with inventory or purchasing teams to resolve them.

D. I have primarily relied on ERP\-generated inventory and material shortage reports to plan production and purchasing.

E. I have not worked in an environment with significant inventory or purchasing record discrepancies.

**Summary:**  

The Senior Finance Analyst, Program Finance owns the financial position of the Enterprise Laboratory Instrument Services (ELIS) program: the profit and loss, the budget cycle, the billing accuracy and the savings the program claims. The seat also owns the arithmetic behind any commercial claim the program makes.  

  

The role reports to the Director of Sourcing and Payments, leads the Finance Analysts, and partners with the Regional Directors of Operations on the regional profit and loss, the Program Analyst on operational analysis, and the Accounts Payable Coordinators on the spend position.  

  

**What you will do:**  

Program profit and loss:  

  

Own the program profit and loss, including labor, parts, travel, tooling and vendor pass\-through.  

  

Own the monthly close for the program, including accruals, prepayments and reconciliation to the general ledger.  

  

Analyze and explain margin performance by region, site and service line.  

  

Own the forecast and the re\-forecast and explain the variance rather than restating it.  

  

Flag margin erosion early, including where delivered scope has grown beyond the priced baseline.  

  

**Billing and revenue:**  

  

Own billing accuracy against the contractual pricing structure, including named headcount, rate lines and pass\-through mechanics.  

  

Confirm every billed line traces to a contractual basis before the invoice is issued.  

  

Own the billing calendar and the resolution of any client query on a billed amount.  

  

Own revenue recognition for the program in line with Renovo policy.  

  

Own the commercial mechanics agreed with the client, including invoicing frequency, payment terms and any float position.  

  

**Commercial case support:**  

  

Own the financial arithmetic behind change orders, material scope changes and pricing proposals.  

  

Build the cost basis for a new or expanded scope from actual loaded cost rather than an assumed rate.  

  

Own the savings baseline, so any saving claimed to the client traces to a prior contract price or prior labor cost.  

  

Model the financial effect of self\-perform and RenovoCare conversion, including the step cost of hiring whole heads against fractional demand.  

  

Provide the financial view in client business reviews and in internal commercial decisions.  

  

**Budget and planning:**  

  

Own the annual budget cycle for the program with the Regional Directors and the sites.  

  

Provide site\-level budget and spend data in a form site leadership can use rather than only report.  

  

Own the headcount cost model, including loaded cost, burden and rate build.  

  

Support workforce and capacity planning with the cost consequence of each option.  

  

**Leading the function and control:**  

  

Lead the Finance Analysts, including work allocation, development and performance management.  

  

Own financial controls for the program, including approval limits and segregation of duties.  

  

Support internal and client audits with traceable financial records.  

  

Maintain the documented method behind every reported financial measure so any figure can be reproduced.  

  

**Qualifications:**  

  

7\+ years of experience in financial analysis, management accounting, commercial finance or program finance.  

  

2\+ years of experience leading a finance team or function.  

  

Demonstrated ownership of a contract or program profit and loss, including monthly close.  

  

Demonstrated experience owning billing accuracy against a contractual pricing structure.  

  

Experience building the cost basis for a change order, pricing proposal or business case from actual loaded cost.  

  

Strong modelling capability, and the discipline to show the arithmetic chain rather than only the result.  

  

Experience with enterprise resource planning and reporting environment.  

  

Experience in a service, outsourcing or regulated technical service environment strongly preferred.  

  

**Education/Special Training:**  

  

Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics or business required. Professional accounting qualification preferred.  

  

Training in GxP, data integrity and client site safety provided or required.  

  

Financial system and CMMS training provided after hire.  

  

**Required Competencies:**  

  

Traceability \- every number can be reproduced and will not be published if it cannot.  

  

Commercial Judgment \- builds a case on actual cost rather than an assumed rate.  

  

Billing Rigor \- confirms the contractual basis before the invoice goes out.  

  

Early Warning \- flags margin erosion while it can still be acted on.  

  

People Leadership \- develops analysts and holds the standard on method.  

  

Practicality \- gives operations a number they can act on, not only a report.  

  

Communication \- explains a financial position to operations and an operational reality to finance leadership.  

  

Integrity \- can admit mistakes, is direct and truthful, and acts in the best interest of clients, employees and Renovo.  

  

**Success Measures:**  

  

Program profit and loss against plan  

  

Margin performance by region, site and service line  

  

Monthly close completed on schedule and reconciled

Understand how the work is performed well enough to recognize a figure that cannot be true and investigate rather than publish it.  

  

State the limitations of any analysis, including sample size, data gaps and known record defects affecting the result.  

  

Distinguish correlation from cause and say which one an analysis supports.  

  

Refuse to present a threshold rule or heuristic as a statistical conclusion.  

  

Reconcile any figure appearing in more than one report so the program does not publish two different answers to the same question.

**Responsibilities:**


***Migration Architecture and Data Mapping***  

* Assess the legacy Microsoft Project Web Access environment and produce a defensible mapping of every legacy data element to its P6 destination, including activity codes, user\-defined fields, WBS levels, calendars, or planned retirement, with rationale documented and Government\-approved.
* Design the enterprise architecture, including EPS hierarchy, WBS standards, activity coding dictionary, calendar library, and UDF strategy sized for portfolio\-scale reporting.

* Convert milestone\-dominant legacy records into activities with durations and logic while preserving genuine milestones and maintaining legacy reporting during parallel operations until the Government accepts the new reporting.
* Establish and routinely report schedule health criteria, including open ends, negative lag, constraint use, out\-of\-sequence progress, excessive float, and missing predecessors or successors.

***Master Schedule Development, Integration, and Variance Analysis***  

* Build and manage master schedules with full traceability of program and project milestones defined by SEP federal program managers.

* Develop training aids, job aids, bulletins, quick\-reference guides, and SOPs, and provide recurring instruction through office hours, working sessions, recorded walkthroughs, and cohort training.

* Produce the weekly Capital Integrated Schedule and Risk/Event Report, support Capital Schedule and Variance Reports, and develop executive reporting showing milestone status and variance in clear, non\-technical language.

Before you read a word of this: if you have never run $10,000 a day on an ecommerce account, and cannot show me the screen that proves you did, this is not your job. I will save you five minutes.

If you have, keep reading, because the rest of this post is written for you.

**WHAT WE SELL**

A garnet bracelet, to women over sixty who have quietly stopped believing a man will ever cross a room for them again. Direct to consumer. Meta is the engine, Google runs brand and product search behind it, a quiz funnel does the selling. We spend six figures a month and we are scaling into Q4 right now, which is why this seat exists.

**HOW WE WIN, SO YOU KNOW WHAT YOU ARE WALKING INTO**

Creative is the lever. We do not win on audience tricks or bid hacks, we win because one ad out of a batch becomes a breakthrough and we know how to find it, prove it and scale it. Our best ad right now is an eleven\-minute talk from a stage, built from a nine\-and\-a\-half\-thousand\-word story that reads at a third\-grade level, and it was built out of 400 post\-purchase survey responses we read line by line.

Your job is the other half of that machine. Clean reads. Kill rules set before launch, not in the moment. Scaling the winner without giving back the efficiency. Catching the account problem, the payment hold, the disapproval, the pixel wobble, before it costs a day of Q4\. And telling me the truth about the numbers, especially when the truth is that my favorite ad is losing.

You do not need to know our system on day one. You need to be willing to learn it fast and argue with it in numbers.

**WHAT YOU WOULD ACTUALLY DO**

\- Run the Meta account every day: budgets, launches, kills, scaling. Highest\-volume bidding is our default at this stage; you will be expected to know when that stops being true and to prove it.

\- Launch every creative batch on our tracking codes so every order tells us which ad, which hook and which sale label produced it, and read the results by cost per purchase per cell, not by the dashboard's daily mood.

\- Set the kill rules in writing before a test goes live, so decisions are arithmetic. Use a rolling efficiency floor as the guardrail, because daily ROAS lies while attribution backfills.

\- Design tests that read cleanly: champion against challenger, one variable at a time, never two new things launched on the same day.

\- Scale winners: the budget steps, the campaign duplication, the audience widening, the frequency watch, and the moment to stop. You have done this through at least one Q4 and you remember what broke first.

\- Own the money side of the account with me: spend against cash reserves, spend against stock (our sale reasons are literally true and match inventory, always), spend against the Google brand search that catches what Meta starts.

\- Sit in the creative meeting. You bring the numbers, the comment sections and the hook\-recall data; you help pick what gets built next. Media buyers here have a say in creative because the creative is where the money is.

\- Report weekly in one page: spend, purchases, cost per purchase, blended efficiency, cash, stock days, and what you would do next with the same money.

**WHO THIS IS NOT FOR**

\- You cannot show proof of $10,000 a day or more, on an ecommerce brand, with the dates visible.

\- You have only ever run accounts inside an agency where someone else made the final call and someone else made the creative.

\- Your first explanation for a bad week is the creative, the pixel or the algorithm, in that order, every time.

\- You believe in cost caps, interest stacking, lookalike ladders or any other structure as a matter of faith rather than as a thing you tested against the alternative in the last twelve months.

\- You have never had an account restricted, an ad disapproved or a payment held, or you have and you cannot tell me what you did in the first hour.

\- You want to be left alone with the account. I read the numbers every day. You will be asked what they mean, often.

**WHO THIS IS FOR**

\- You have scaled an ecommerce account past $10K a day and held it there, and you can show the screen.

\- You know why daily ROAS is unreliable and what you look at instead.

\- You write your kill rules down before launch and you can name the last ad you killed on the rule while it still looked fine to everyone else.

\- You have watched an account break under scale, you know what broke, and you fixed it.

\- You want to learn direct response from the inside: the survey file, the sealed copy laws, why a nine\-thousand\-word ad outperforms a thirty\-second one for this customer. You are hungry for that, not tolerant of it.

\- You would rather be right in thirty days at real spend than sound smart on a call.

**WHAT IT PAYS**

Base: $70K/year, set by the proof you bring, not by the interview.

Then the part that matters:

\- A monthly bonus tied to blended efficiency held at scale. You get paid for spending more at the same cost per purchase, not for spending less.

\- A quarterly bonus tied to blended customer acquisition cost across every channel, the number that decides whether this business works.

\- Profit share at the next step up, written into the offer letter with the exact trigger.

**WHERE IT GOES**

This is the first buyer seat in a company that intends to build a growth department, not a seat under an agency. Hold efficiency through one full Q4 at higher spend and you are Senior Media Buyer. Own every paid channel with cost per purchase flat or down for two consecutive quarters and you are Head of Growth, with a budget you allocate across Meta, Google, TikTok and email, a profit share, and hires you choose. The triggers are written down so nobody moves up on tenure or charm, only on numbers that held.

**HOW TO APPLY. READ THIS PART CAREFULLY. IT IS THE FIRST TEST.**

No cover letter. No certifications list. I will not read either.

Apply here on Indeed and put three things in the message box:

1\. Proof.

**Preferred Qualifications**

new_jobs.description:
Before you read a word of this: if you have never run $10,000 a day on an ecommerce account, and cannot show me the screen that proves you did, this is not your job. I will save you five minutes.

If you have, keep reading, because the rest of this post is written for you.

**WHAT WE SELL**

A garnet bracelet, to women over sixty who have quietly stopped believing a man will ever cross a room for them again. Direct to consumer. Meta is the engine, Google runs brand and product search behind it, a quiz funnel does the selling. We spend six figures a month and we are scaling into Q4 right now, which is why this seat exists.

**HOW WE WIN, SO YOU KNOW WHAT YOU ARE WALKING INTO**

Creative is the lever. We do not win on audience tricks or bid hacks, we win because one ad out of a batch becomes a breakthrough and we know how to find it, prove it and scale it. Our best ad right now is an eleven\-minute talk from a stage, built from a nine\-and\-a\-half\-thousand\-word story that reads at a third\-grade level, and it was built out of 400 post\-purchase survey responses we read line by line.

Your job is the other half of that machine. Clean reads. Kill rules set before launch, not in the moment. Scaling the winner without giving back the efficiency. Catching the account problem, the payment hold, the disapproval, the pixel wobble, before it costs a day of Q4\. And telling me the truth about the numbers, especially when the truth is that my favorite ad is losing.

You do not need to know our system on day one. You need to be willing to learn it fast and argue with it in numbers.

**WHAT YOU WOULD ACTUALLY DO**

\- Run the Meta account every day: budgets, launches, kills, scaling. Highest\-volume bidding is our default at this stage; you will be expected to know when that stops being true and to prove it.

\- Launch every creative batch on our tracking codes so every order tells us which ad, which hook and which sale label produced it, and read the results by cost per purchase per cell, not by the dashboard's daily mood.

\- Set the kill rules in writing before a test goes live, so decisions are arithmetic. Use a rolling efficiency floor as the guardrail, because daily ROAS lies while attribution backfills.

\- Design tests that read cleanly: champion against challenger, one variable at a time, never two new things launched on the same day.

\- Scale winners: the budget steps, the campaign duplication, the audience widening, the frequency watch, and the moment to stop. You have done this through at least one Q4 and you remember what broke first.

\- Own the money side of the account with me: spend against cash reserves, spend against stock (our sale reasons are literally true and match inventory, always), spend against the Google brand search that catches what Meta starts.

\- Sit in the creative meeting. You bring the numbers, the comment sections and the hook\-recall data; you help pick what gets built next. Media buyers here have a say in creative because the creative is where the money is.

\- Report weekly in one page: spend, purchases, cost per purchase, blended efficiency, cash, stock days, and what you would do next with the same money.

**WHO THIS IS NOT FOR**

\- You cannot show proof of $10,000 a day or more, on an ecommerce brand, with the dates visible.

\- You have only ever run accounts inside an agency where someone else made the final call and someone else made the creative.

\- Your first explanation for a bad week is the creative, the pixel or the algorithm, in that order, every time.

\- You believe in cost caps, interest stacking, lookalike ladders or any other structure as a matter of faith rather than as a thing you tested against the alternative in the last twelve months.

\- You have never had an account restricted, an ad disapproved or a payment held, or you have and you cannot tell me what you did in the first hour.

\- You want to be left alone with the account. I read the numbers every day. You will be asked what they mean, often.

**WHO THIS IS FOR**

\- You have scaled an ecommerce account past $10K a day and held it there, and you can show the screen.

\- You know why daily ROAS is unreliable and what you look at instead.

\- You write your kill rules down before launch and you can name the last ad you killed on the rule while it still looked fine to everyone else.

\- You have watched an account break under scale, you know what broke, and you fixed it.

\- You want to learn direct response from the inside: the survey file, the sealed copy laws, why a nine\-thousand\-word ad outperforms a thirty\-second one for this customer. You are hungry for that, not tolerant of it.

\- You would rather be right in thirty days at real spend than sound smart on a call.

**WHAT IT PAYS**

Base: $70K/year, set by the proof you bring, not by the interview.

Then the part that matters:

\- A monthly bonus tied to blended efficiency held at scale. You get paid for spending more at the same cost per purchase, not for spending less.

\- A quarterly bonus tied to blended customer acquisition cost across every channel, the number that decides whether this business works.

\- Profit share at the next step up, written into the offer letter with the exact trigger.

**WHERE IT GOES**

This is the first buyer seat in a company that intends to build a growth department, not a seat under an agency. Hold efficiency through one full Q4 at higher spend and you are Senior Media Buyer. Own every paid channel with cost per purchase flat or down for two consecutive quarters and you are Head of Growth, with a budget you allocate across Meta, Google, TikTok and email, a profit share, and hires you choose. The triggers are written down so nobody moves up on tenure or charm, only on numbers that held.

**HOW TO APPLY. READ THIS PART CAREFULLY. IT IS THE FIRST TEST.**

No cover letter. No certifications list. I will not read either.

Apply here on Indeed and put three things in the message box:

1\. Proof.
